resolved_finding.problem: Initial candidate acquired and returned a live in_channel from off_fiber, installing caller Fun.protect only after delivery. No channel cleanup was scoped inside acquire worker. Repeated cancellations could leave FD release to eventual GC rather than completed structured cleanup. This applied to actual fiber/pool path, not inline/already-worker paths; not claimed executed reproduction.

assessments.topic: Partial EOF and suffix lower bound
assessments.result: Suffix starts at previous size only when previous extent ended in newline and same-inode append successor holds. That is a physical row boundary; scan_step lower_bound never reads old prefix and preserves newest-first callback application. No selected new suffix falls back only to same-file previous value. Incomplete old tail forces full rescan, retaining original strict latest behavior of decoding a valid unterminated JSON row; newline completeness is an incremental-reuse condition, not a new rule excluding all unterminated rows.

Uncached scan captures size, bounds read until it, and checks same snapshot on final handle and current path plus actual last byte before caching. Changed file yields explicit Read_file error and no new map publication. I/O catch shape preserves cancellation propagation; outer protect closes on errors/callback exceptions. Existing strict API catches Sys_error/Invalid_argument/EOF around callbacks too; this review does not broaden exception policy. No new catch-all/retry/default or authority fallback.

Mutex copies/publishes immutable map only; no lock held over I/O/callback. Older concurrent publication can regress cache metadata and cause another scan, but next actual file witness prevents blind stale reuse; append-only fallback rescans needed suffix. Cancellation/errors do not publish visited map. Consumer invalidation removes old view from global table; in-flight holder cannot reinsert it.256store cap remains; no global cache added inside Dated.

View keeps fixed store/project closure, per-visited-file stats/completeness and selected value or None; no decoded-row list/source-byte buffer retained by scanner itself. Generic value type may itself retain whatever caller returns, so no unconditional arbitrary-callback graph-release theorem. Actual tool audit retains only selected tool strings/count/source/timestamp fields and path-bound reporting closure. Number of None/stat entries scales with files visited until match;256consumer cap is a store cap, not a per-file memory bound.

Opaque new latest_view API is additive; existing scan helper callers keep default lower_bound0 and unchanged signatures externally. Actual consumer loses full retained count and uses fixed per-path view. Added maintained cases specify sparse None reuse, only appended callback visits, same-file fallback, partial EOF completion, replacement/truncation, cached older-file symlink error, and same-count official metrics rotation/prune. They are source-inspected intentions, not passing receipts.
